title: Ben Duckett Smashes 141 as England Pile Pressure on India in Series-Deciding Lord's Test
excerpt: The left-hander's aggressive century anchors England's second-innings fightback at the Home of Cricket, where the five-match series hangs in the balance.
body:
• Ben Duckett scored a commanding 141 in England's second innings at Lord's, his highest Test score against India.
  • The five-match series is locked at 1-1 heading into the decisive third Test at the Home of Cricket, after India won the second Test at The Oval and the first at Old Trafford was drawn.
  • Harry Brook complemented Duckett with a century of his own (111 off 98 balls) in the second innings at The Oval, but it was not enough to prevent India's victory.
  • India's bowling attack, led by Jasprit Bumrah, faces its toughest challenge yet as England's batsmen find form at the series' most pivotal moment.

Ben Duckett chose the biggest stage in cricket to play the innings of his life.

The left-handed opener hammered 141 at Lord's in the series-deciding third Test against India, anchoring England's second innings with a display of aggressive, purposeful batting that has put the hosts in a commanding position.

Series on a Knife Edge

The five-match series arrived at Lord's perfectly poised. The first Test at Old Trafford ended in a draw, with England posting a mammoth 669 in the first innings — Zak Crawley scoring 84 and Brydon Carse contributing 47 — before India's second-innings resistance, anchored by a collective effort that saw them reach 425 for 4, ran out the clock.

India then seized the initiative at The Oval in the second Test, chasing down 396 to win despite centuries from Duckett and Brook. It was a result that demonstrated the depth and determination of India's batting lineup, with Gus Atkinson's five-wicket haul in the first innings proving insufficient for England.

Now at Lord's, with the series at 1-1, Duckett's 141 has given England the platform they need.

Duckett's Dominance

The Nottinghamshire batter, who has established himself as one of England's most reliable openers in the Bazball era, was at his aggressive best. His innings featured powerful driving through the covers and characteristic sweeps against India's spinners, building partnerships that wore down an Indian bowling attack that had looked formidable at The Oval.

India's pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, who took two wickets in the first innings at The Oval and bowled 33 overs with an economy rate of 3.39 at Old Trafford, faces the challenge of breaking through on a Lord's surface that has offered less assistance than The Oval.

India's Challenge

For India, the series represents a crucial test of their overseas credentials. The touring squad, captained by the experienced core of KL Rahul, Shubman Gill, and Ravindra Jadeja, showed in their Oval victory that they can chase big totals in English conditions. Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sai Sudharsan have provided youthful energy in the batting order, while Washington Sundar and Jadeja offer spin options that could prove decisive on a wearing Lord's pitch.

The absence of Rishabh Pant from the Lord's squad — after his contributions at Old Trafford — adds intrigue to India's selection decisions for the remainder of the series.

What's at Stake

For the millions of Indian cricket fans in the UK who fill English grounds with chants of "India, India," this series carries enormous emotional weight. A series win in England remains one of the most coveted achievements in Indian cricket, and with the series alive heading into the final two Tests, every session at Lord's matters.

Duckett's 141 has raised the stakes. India's response will determine whether this series becomes another chapter in England's home dominance or India's growing legacy as conquerors of English conditions.
